lead.headline: Max wins in Singapore at the tenth attempt, after leading every session of the weekend
lead.short: From pole he beat Leclerc by 7.3 seconds, with Antonelli third and the McLarens fourth and fifth; he had also topped sprint qualifying, the sprint and qualifying. Ferrari were heading for second and third until Hamilton overrode the pit wall, stayed out on fading tyres and fell to sixth, then apologised on the radio: "My call, and I lost us valuable points." Singapore had been one of the two tracks on the calendar where Max had never won.
more: Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points with six races and 150 points left, and could clinch the title in Austin on 25 October.
lead.highlight: My call, and I lost us valuable points

why.text: Two wins in two races: Max's season has turned, though the title is Antonelli's to lose.

update.front: Max winning in Singapore for the first time leads the paper for this reader.

seconds.headline: Saturday's strike on Riyadh airport killed 13, including an Indian man; another hit on Sunday killed one
seconds.short: The Saturday attack on King Khalid International also injured 308, the deadliest single strike on a Gulf Arab country since the war began in February; the Indian embassy said an Indian man died of his injuries. On Sunday a projectile set fire to a passenger hall and killed a Pakistani resident. The Houthis say every Saudi airport except those of Mecca and Medina is a target; the Saudi-led coalition has vowed to respond.

why.text: Riyadh is a major hub for Indians working in the Gulf, and the embassy has told nationals to stay alert.

update.new: A far deadlier strike on Saturday, with an Indian among the dead.
update.front: The deadliest attack on a Gulf state in this war, with an Indian killed, is front-page news.

seconds.headline: Delhi Police strike Jantar Mantar off the list of protest sites and name three grounds instead
seconds.byline: THE HINDU · HINDUSTAN TIMES · INDIAN EXPRESS · 12 OCT
seconds.short: Protests will now be allowed at Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and the CBD Ground in east Delhi, on the recommendation of a Home Ministry committee. The order came on the day the INDIA bloc planned its march; Kerala's Assembly passed a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal.

why.text: The capital's best-known protest site, a few hundred metres from Parliament, is closed to protest days after the Supreme Court told police to respect the right.

update.new: Jantar Mantar de-notified as a protest venue; Kerala's Assembly asks for the CEC's removal.
update.front: Closing Jantar Mantar to protest is a change in how Delhi works, not just another day of the dispute.

seconds.headline: Abhishek's 69 from 30 balls and Arshdeep's three wickets put India 2–1 up
seconds.short: India made 223 and held West Indies to 209 for 7 to win by 14 runs in Indore. Abhishek became the fastest to 2,000 T20I runs, and Arshdeep, player of the match, took 3 for 44, including Shai Hope for the first time. The fourth match is in Hyderabad on Wednesday and the fifth in Bengaluru on Saturday.

monday.mood: The Sensex was down about 0.8% at 14:00, having fallen more than 1,000 points from the day's high, as Asian markets weakened and oil stayed high after the weekend's attacks in the Gulf. Banks and IT led the fall, with Airtel, ICICI Bank, Reliance and SBI the biggest drags; the RBI's new curbs on dollar hedging began to bite.
weekend: On Saturday the RBI announced a 20% cash reserve on large import hedges, a ban on rebooking cancelled rupee contracts and a direct dollar window for the state oil companies from today.
A strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 on Saturday, and the Houthis threatened every Saudi airport, keeping oil high.
Trump announced a Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' after easing sanctions on Russian diesel; Kyiv says attacks continue, and Iran rejected the latest US response on reopening Hormuz.
September SIPs set a record at ₹32,490 crore even as foreign investors kept selling.
